61982.question_text: What would be observed when aqueous ammonia is added in drops and then in excess to a solution of copper(II) ions?
61982.explanation:
When a few drops of ammonia solution is added to copper(II) ions, a blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide is formed.
CuSO₄(aq) + 2NH₃(aq) + 2H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ Cu(OH)₂(s) + (NH₄)₂SO₄(aq)
However, when ammonia solution is added in excess, the blue precipitate re-dissolves to form a deep blue solution of tetraamine copper(II) hydroxide.
Cu(OH)₂(s) + 4NH₃(aq) → [Cu(NH₃)₄](OH)₂(aq). Therefore, the correct answer is option A.

62104.question_text:
The following ions have the same electron configuration except 

\(_{8}\)O, \(_{12}\)Mg, \(_{13}\)AI, \(_{17}\)CI
62104.explanation:
Electron Count Verification

To determine which ion does not share the same electron configuration, we calculate the number of electrons for each given ion using the formula:
Number of Electrons = Atomic Number - Charge

Option A: Cl\(^-\)

The atomic number of Chlorine (Cl) is 17. 

A -1 charge means it has gained 1 electron.

Total electrons = 17 - (-1) = 18 electrons 

(Configuration: 1s\(^2\)2s\(^2\)2p\(^6\)3s\(^2\)3p\(^6\), matching Argon).

  • Total electrons = \(17 - (-1) = \mathbf{18\text{ electrons}}\) (Configuration: \(1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}\), matching Argon). [1]
